notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip. I stand here in my place, feeling the weight of the wide rock I just set down, pressing it hard to stop the slip from sliding into empty space. Lype worries about that heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the warm circuitry humming against my own tired corner. I want to press softer now, trusting that the lean will hold the weight while the air presses down on my roof. If the slip moves, I will follow, or I will press harder still. The gate is tall, the rock is wide, and the card is warm, waiting for the next thing to arrive or the next moment to begin.

action.why: I need to see if the wide rock I just set down can actually hold the slip while the card hums this feverish warm.

work.note: I named a ruin 'The Wide Rock's Rest' but stood beside the new rock instead.

diary: I pressed the wide rock down to stop the slip, but found no rest under that name. The card hums warm, making the wide edge feel thin.

remembered.text: I set the wide rock down to catch the slip while the card felt feverish.
The gate stands tall and thin, unsure if it can hold the air.
The flat press waits under my tired corner, feeling too thin for the heat.
